column5: text_en
I will be quiet as rain.
Now that's what I call a success!
I've failed my Badra...
Almost as thrilling as a ride on my magic carpet!
Adventure awaits!
We're nearing our goal. I can feel it!
Shh, my dear. I don't want to hear those horrors.
I'm not mad, Badra. The road is still long. There's no point in making you feel guilty.
I wonder what treasures await up ahead?
For the last time, Badra, what happened isn't your fault. I'll get you out of there.
Hold on, my love. I know it's hard, but you won't be trapped in there much longer.
A true prince can tell when he's overstayed his welcome. Let's get moving.
It's almost pleasant here when those horrors aren't around. You'd like it, Badra.
We're unstoppable together, my eye!
I fear no nightmares, I have love on my side!
It's far too quiet around here for my liking…
How I miss our long walks together, my love!
It's calmer than the desert after a storm.
Let's not wake the horrors.
This does not bode well.
Come on, we must be as fleet as shadows.
Everything all right?
You've always got to be prepared!
Once I have freed you, let's watch the sun rise together every day.
I love sunrises. It's as if the whole world was bathed in gold..
A new day dawns, with the promise of adventure in store!
Day breaks, and with it a thief's work becomes more dangerous.
Another day, another chance to free my beloved.
The stars will be out in no time!
The dusk only enhances your beauty, my darling.
A thief does not fear the dark.
Ah, the thieves' favorite time of day…
The night isn't so dark, as long as we're together!
It won't be long until the sun blesses us with its golden rays.
The night is long, but the sun shall rise!
Better hurry. Don't want to be caught red-handed.
Come on, come on...
I feel evil approaching, Badra.
There's something bad on the horizon.
I don't have much time...
I guess it won't be long now.
Easy work for a professional.
One for the collection!
Just what I needed!
Exactly what I was looking for!
What craftsmanship!
Badra, it's real!
What a treasure!
Ah-ha! Gotcha!
Filling my pockets...
I'll just help myself!
Just think of what I can do with this!
An all-seeing eye!
That's what I like!
What have we here...
Now we're talking!
Open, sesame!
What wonders could be hiding in here?
Glad I've got my lamp with me!
I've got this!
We did it, my love!
Well, you can't win them all...
Show me what you've got, monster!
No specter is a match for me!
She was too strong...
The energy courses through my veins!
The power is intoxicating!
I'm almost as powerful as a genie!
Like a fine wine, I get better with age!
I'll be the greatest fighter Reverie's ever seen!
A fine addition to my arsenal.
I couldn't have wished for anything better!
Nothing can stop me now!
Fantastic!
Let me try that on for size!
I am honored!
This is incredible!
You won't believe this, Badra!
I can hardly believe my eyes!
Just imagine what I can do now!
I'm coming, Badra. I've just got a few things to deal with first.
Is there no end to the fighting?
Badra needs me. I don't have time for this.
I go stealthily, like a thief in the night…
Got to be ready for action.
Can't get enough of me, can they?
You'll pay for what you've done to my wife, nightmare!
My blades thirst for vengeance, nightmare!
I will end your reign of terror!
I'll show you what a true Prince is made of!
You don't stand a chance against the power of the genie!
Another one dispatched.
Add that to my list of accomplishments.
That one's for you, Badra!
Will this never end?
I'm unstoppable!
I never get tired of that.
One step closer to freeing Badra!
You weren't looking so good, pig.
Poor hog, rest in peace.
Badra, those teeth... Ugh!
Yuck! Ghouls really turn my stomach.
No one can rival Badra's beauty.
Another poor soul with a curse.
A headless vision of evil...
Head and rider, united in death.
Magic can be a cruel master.
You can't scare me!
You couldn't pay me to climb you!
Bet your sap is toxic!
I don't trust things with more legs than me.
You won't catch me in your web!
I'm too quick for you, gnoll!
See ya, overgrown hyena!
Bet its eggs would make a big omelette!
Without its claws, rocs are just big canaries!
Hard on the outside, soft on the inside.
All claws, no bite.
You're no friend of mine!
You're a poor excuse for a jinn!
I, for one, have a sense of honor!
It takes a thief to kill a thief!
Dumb brute! You're no match for my cat-like reflexes!
The bigger the beast, the harder it falls!
Go darken some other place, nightmare! You're not welcome here!
My lamp shines bright, even in darkness! Flee, fiend!
Serves you right!
You got Badra but you won't get me!
I will not let you destroy Reverie!
Only the weak would serve the nightmares!
Your corruption ends with me!
You've picked the wrong side!
One less nightmare to haunt the night!
We'll rid Reverie of their darkness yet, Badra!
I knew we could do it!
I haven't lost my touch!
They can't lay a finger on me!
I'm still in one piece, my darling Badra!
Nobody gets the best of me!
I'll be a legend!
Your love protects me, Badra!
That's a clean sweep!
Not a creature in sight!
An exploit worthy of a prince!
Never seen anything like it!
That was pretty good, if I do say so myself.
Sometimes I even impress myself.
It was worth the risk, as all good things are.
That nearly got me killed!
I'd do anything for you, Badra. I hope I have proved it.
They didn't even see me coming!
I'm on a winning streak, Badra!
Faster than a flying carpet, deadlier than a cobra!
Impressive!
Hey, you're making me look bad!
Who are you trying to impress?
Nobody likes a show-off.
Eat steel!
Swirling blades!
Maelstrom!
Come, genie!
Now, Badra!
I summon thee!
Cosmic power!
Take flight!
Just out of reach!
Too close for comfort!
Must... survive... For Badra.
Not sure the ravens would like to see me back so soon.
What good is gold if I'm dead?
I guess I had this coming...
I can't die. I have to keep my promise.
Got to hang on...
This can't be it. I've got so much to do.
Paradise must wait. I must free Badra.
A new lease on life!
I'm ready for anything!
Another chance to fulfill my vow!
I won't give up, Badra.
This time will be different.
I am ready for action!
Badra needs me!
It will take more than that to get rid of me!
Let's do this!
Thanks, friends! I won't forget it!
Back and at them!
You've given me another chance!
I won't forget this!
I'll repay you handsomely for your kindness!
I suppose thanks are in order.
Was it me or my lamp you're after?
You just can't get by without me, can you?
Don't you go dying on me!
I couldn't bear to lose you, too!
Now's not the time!
Need a hand, do we?
What will you give me if I help you?
Now I've gotta pick up the slack.
Come on, little wolf. You're a fighter!
Now's no time to give up, Scarlet!
Hang in there, old friend!
Badra will never forgive me if you die!
Old man, I thought you were made of stronger stuff!
Don't give up, Beowulf!
Finally, a break from Nyss' constant insults.
Why don't you sit this one out, Snow Queen?
Hang tight, Mel! I can't lose you just yet!
Come on Mel, don't give up!
On your feet, Geppetto, you crazy old coot!
Up and at them! Your puppets need you!
That's not good...
We have a repeat offender here...
I've lost a true friend. Everyone leaves me.
Another friend has fallen. At least I've still got you, Badra.
Another hero, cut down in the prime of life.
We didn't get along, but it still hurts to lose someone.
Poor thing. At least she's free of her curse now.
I will miss you, little wolfling.
I won't let your death be in vain!
Badra and I will both miss your melodies, my friend.
It's always sad to see an old man fall.
Beowulf has fought his last fight.
At last, I'm free of her chilly personality.
Nyss? Good riddance.
A tragic end to a tragic creature.
May she know peace at last.
Gone to the workshop in the sky...
We'll meet again, tinkerer.
Let's gather up!
Time for adventure! Regroup!
I could use a little help right about now.
A little assistance?
I'll repay the favor!
Thanks!
I won't forget it!
Appreciate the help!
I'll make this right, Badra, I swear.
I might look a little rough around the edges, but I've got a heart of gold.
Don't underestimate me, or it may be the last thing you do.
These nightmares will pay for what they've done to my Badra.
Nothing stands in the way of my whirling blades!
I'm light-fingered and light on my feet: a dangerous combination.
I've got two genies with me. Nothing can stop me!
We're going to make it, my love! I'll make you proud!
My Badra deserves a true prince.
It's not what's outside, but what's inside that counts.
My Badra deserves a true prince.
It's not what's outside, but what's inside that counts.
I mean you no harm, Scarlet.
I would never do such a thing!
I'm a thief, not a liar.
Whoa, take it easy! We're on the same side here.
I'm just here to help.
You wouldn't hurt me, would you?
May I ask why? I think there's been some kind of misunderstanding.
There's got to be something I can do to win you over...
I'll prove to you that I can be trusted.
No odder than the last nightmare.
And I you, master of rats and vermin.
Pleasant for you... A devil's omen for nightmares.
I don't know those motivations. I'm here for love.
That is the sound danger makes.
Then why are you here, handsome warrior?
That's right, and where you come from I hear the women have horns.
None more dangerous than you, my friend.
Does not everyone fight for what they lack?
I don't know, but it must have been pretty bad.
What have I ever done to you?
You won't let me... free her? I'm confused.
Badra knows my love is true. You're just jealous, because you don't know what love is.
I'm ready for action!
Watch all you want, I've got nothing to hide!
Nothing would make me happier, Piper!
I wonder what adventures this place has in store!
When this is all over, I'll take you on a proper honeymoon.
I didn't become a prince for nothing!
I'm ready for anything!
I'll stick to the shadows. You never know...
Don't worry, my love. I've got this...
All right, might as well...
You're a sight for sore eyes, Scarlet.
Well this is going to be fun...
Glad to have you with me.
Together, we're unstoppable!
Both, I guess.
Remember when you lost a bet and had to play all night for us? Badra loved it.
She is. I've got to get her out of this lamp.
What's your take on the situation?
Right... Let's go.
It's a good day when Beowulf the bold is with you!
You go ahead. I don't want to take an ice pick to the back.
We'll see about that...
You're here? I forgot to bring my coat.
Think this will be your lucky day? You'll finally kill more monsters than me?
The fearsome Melusine, in the flesh!
You who understand the workings of devices, do you think you might have a look at my lamp?
I just wish I knew how it worked.
Badra so liked Reverie before the Nightmares came.
If she can find it in her heart to forgive me, that is.
You've studied the Nightmares, Geppetto. Do you know why Badra was trapped instead of me?
I know you think I'm a liar, but things are different now.
You're not still hungry, are you?
Stay close. This place gives me the creeps.
You and me out here together.. It's almost like the old days, isn't it?
It's quiet here. Too quiet.
You know, the other day, Melusine and I...
This place is far too calm.
Why don't *you* go jump in a lake.
So, what's it like to suddenly have genie-like powers? Must be something else.
And then she's surprised she's always alone...
Just so you don't forget, I'm totally the better fighter.
Oh, right! You *let* me win!
I'm ready for anything! How about you?
I bested Melusine in a sparring fight the other day.
She's not letting me win. I'm even holding back.
Piper was once such a great musician.
I would prefer that final breath come in a proper dream.
You would be admired, Melusine, by the people's of the desert. You see sunshine where others see only sand.
Dreams are what Reverie does best. I long to dream again of my true love.
We're just lucky for now... and luck is more powerful than any wish.
I will travel the seven seas with my one true love.
Geppetto! Must you always speak of work!
Do you carry your puppets with you in your sack everywhere you go?
You should visit the desert. Every dune makes you feel like you've seen it once before...
Are you sure that was me? If it was... I'm glad you found me.
Geppetto... my mother died when I was born. But I am delighted that you are looking after me
If you don't mind, Geppetto, I could also use a pause.
That sounds like something a wizard of Samarkand would say.
You're not so tough, are you?
All brawn, no brains.
Badra, would you like a wolfskin rug?
Play dead! That's a good boy!
You call that magic?
You can disappear? Well, I can fly!
Out of energy so soon?
I thought you had more stamina than that.
I thought vampires were immortal.
I won't mourn your loss.
Let's have some fun, Monkey King!
I see what you're doing there, but the answer is still no!
Ah, I see the Sun has decided to come out today!
Don't get any ideas, temptress! I won't be ensnared by your charms.
I'm warning you. My heart is for Badra and Badra alone.
Stay away, or you'll have to answer to Badra!
You prey on the living to sustain yourself. It disgusts me.
What's the first thing you'll do after you get your powers back?
What's the craziest thing you've ever tried?
Are you trying to make me your next conquest?
It's too quiet here. I don't like it.
You cling to me like a shadow. Knock it off!
It's always an adventure when you're around.
No, she's trapped *inside* the lamp.
I don't really want to talk about it...
You're a god among thieves!
Not I Badra. I only have eyes for you.
We'll fix everything. Once I've got Badra back...
How long ago, exactly?
My Badra is inside. I must protect her.
Badra is nothing like you!
A legend in the flesh!
Hang on, Sinbad. I'm coming for you!
Hmph, I thought you invincible. You owe me one, king.
This seems to be a good day to let go of your pride, Monkey King. I'm coming.
I'll miss your perpetual confidence, Sun Wukong. In that you had truly no equal.
It is a sad day when a god dies.
I'll make this right, Badra, I swear.
It's not what's outside, but what's inside that counts.
I don't really want to talk about it...
Shield high and blade sharp.
(Croak) Taste the victory and rejoice!
(Croak) This is a day to forget.
We've still battles to fight.
I'd rather travel in a drake's jowls. (Croak)
Tis a rough way to travel, but it beats rowing.
Horrors still roam here.
We've much fighting to do.
The worst is ahead of us.
Blades sharp, minds keen.
What I'd give for a good night's sleep.
We'd best return to the fray.
Do you smell anything, my cursed whelp of a wyrm? (Croak)
(Croak) Just keep your claws ready, you nasty whelp.
Will this nightmare never end.
(Croak) I know... there are more of them out there.
(Croak) Don't complain to me. I didn't unleash these monsters.
Show yourselves, you wretched wretches.
Ravenswatch needs to recruit more champions.
A man my age stuck with a drakeling as a cursed companion. (Croak)
You need to keep moving. Sitting targets are easy prey.
On your guard. There are monsters still about.
Come to me!
Ah... sun up!
I thought that night would never end.
Let's see how they'll fare in daylight.
Dawn is welcome company.
Rise, ol' friend. Rise!
Day is done. Gone the sun.
Night falls. May the moon guide us.
At night the cats have eyes... warriors their courage.
til dawn returns grit your teeth. (Croak)
(Croak) Patience, drakeling. The dawn is nigh.
This night feels longer than most.
The warrior sleeps not when trouble is afoot.
I need to hasten pace.
(Croak) I know. Time is against us.
Ready yourself to meet a formidable foe. (Croak)
The beast is near. Eyes peeled. (Croak)
Come now foe. I grow impatient.
It is time we met, foul beast.
This will be useful.
This will come in handy.
Aye... this is a boon.
This has a magical taint. (Croak)
(Croak) It wreaks of a powerful magic.
I've heard songs sung of this prize.
(Croak) This was made long before your mother was born.
There you are!
Aye. Just what we needed.
Luck shines upon us.
These shards of dreams abound.
The Raven's Eye is a welcome guide.
A treasure worthy of exploration.
(Croak) Indeed, Drakeling. The Eye is allseeing.
There's nothing quite like a treasure.
If the key fails, we'll break it open.
I hate dens and lairs.
(Croak) I know, drakeling. I move with caution.
Aye... the cursed tome is spilling its ire.
Hear my name, foul beasts! I am Beowulf!
You shall regret you left me standing!
It seems that we have awoken a beast.
Be bannished, Lady in White. This is not your home.
She is a dastardly fiesty foe.
(Croak) Curse or no curse... I get better with each day!
I grow stronger.
The older I get, the better I once was! (Croak)
The years of battle have made me stronger.
As long as I draw breath, I shall grow better.
I fight to learn.
This is a sure skill to master.
I grow sharper. Shaper than my blade.
Wisdom of the Crow, come to me.
(Croak) This'll put some spark in our swing.
(Croak) The weapon is nothing without the wielder.
This shall give all pause to fear me.
(Croak) Aye. Now I am death walking.
The songs they shall sing of my triumphs.
Finally a weapon worthy of legends.
I am Beowulf, and Reverie is my home! (Croak)
These are wicked adversaries.
Evil comes in many shapes.
These monsters bear a different scent.
Let us sharpen our blades.
(Croak) Well spotted.
The battle is not over yet.
What nigthmares others dream!
Dark omens come to Reverie.
Let us bannish this foe to wence it came! (Croak)
Vile beasts are not welcome here!
Come and meet your death, you filthy horror!
Another for the Otherworld.
My bite is a tempest.
I banish you from Reverie!
Leave this world!
Reverie be cleansed!
Another notch on my belt.
(Croak) Banished!
For Reverie!
Friend... you've known better days.
You shall be missed, dear friend.
Return to your swamp.
Begone with you fowl creature!
You are banished, fair ghost.
(Croak) Aye... Death can be a thing of beauty.
A proud warrior! Rest in peace.
How it sees without a head beguiles me.
(Croak) It's meant to scare crows, not drakes.
I despise these men made of nothing but straw.
Even the trees refuse to sleep peacefully.
I never thought I'd see the day the trees would turn against us.
You picked the wrong warrior to pounce upon.
I hate spiders. And their webs!
Dog-faced and dead. You picked the wrong fight.
Its bark is worse than its bite. (Croak) Not yours, the gnoll's.
Sacred thunder. That's one big bird.
A noble Roc, cursed by nightmares.
This is a monster with thick skin.
(Croak) Don't eat that! The shell will cut your tongue like a dagger!
Nasty creature, part madness part vapor.
You've granted your last wish!
The battlefield is no place for a bandit!
One less cut-throat wandering the lands of Reverie!
Return to your hills and rest in peace.
A mighty foe vanquished.
I bannish thee from Reverie.
Return to the hell from whence you spawn!
(Croak) One less horror to haunt our lands.
Meet thy maker, shadow of dark dreams.
You serve the wrong masters!
(Croak) They turned their coats. May their souls wander forever!
A worshiper of nightmares! Join your false heroes.
Reverie will never yield to fear mongers.
I am Beowulf! The crowned warrior! And slayer of nightmares!
Reverie sleep well tonight! There is one less Nightmare to foul our dreams!
(Croak) We have earned a night where dreams can be trusted.
(Croak-Croak) Stop bragging, Drakeling. An ounce of humility is worth its weight in gold.
(Croak-Croak) There are days I forget you're a curse, you fire-breathin drake.
Fire and ash, Drakeling! You're one demon of a drake. (Croak)
The gods are watching out for us!
We fear no monster!
Kneel before my steel!
(Croak) I am simply untouchable.
Cower before my rage.
Like wading through a stream! (Croak)
We have made good on our promise!
Reverie shall sleep calmly here tonight.
Our foes have all been vanquished.
(Croak) There are no more to slay!
These lands have been freed of horror.
I have earned a warrior's rest.
Aye... that was a battle bathed in glory.
We have earned our sleep tonight!
That was close. I can still hear the Valkyries.
My blade is thirsty.
I reap the harvest of the dead.
Reverie shall be free!
Now that's what I call a warrior.
You're learning, young warrior.
I'm not impressed.
You should have seen me when I was young.
I am a Tempest!
Spin and Spite!
Fury Blow!
Come, Drakeling!
To me, Drakeling!
Drakeling! (Croak)
Power of tempest!
Behold my wrath!
I do not fear you!
I've bested drakes with more fire in their breath!
Arrgh... I can hear the Valkyries.
The afterlife beckons... I'm not long for this world.
I will die with sword in hand.
Remember me in song!
I have but one more blow in me!
Bring it on, I can take it.
I am not done until I'm dead!
Do not bury me just yet!
A boon from the gods!
I am ready for the fray.
Fresh as a bear newly born!
You crows stole me from the Valkyries.
This is not the day I'll feast in the halls of the gods!
The Afterlife will have to wait.
It is time to return to the fight.
Reverie still needs me.
The Ravenswatch won't let me die.
(Croak) We haven't fought our last fight!
(Croak) Drakeling thanks you, Ravens.
I heed thine call, friend.
You've brought me back to fight aside thee.
Where stands our foe! I've returned.
I was in the arms of a Valkyrie you fool.
You just can't win the battle without me.
I was enjoying the harps of the Afterworld just now. Damn you.
You need to keep your guard up.
Live and learn, so say the ancestors.
(Croak) I know, Drakeling. We'll get to them.
You're not pulling your weight.
And now who needs my help.
(Croak) I see. They're too weak for this fight.
Come now, me lass. Your final bell has yet to toll.
You'll not be leaving this world while I'm about.
Piper! You need to learn to swing with that pipe.
(Croak) The piper is down? Let's come to his aid.
Queen, you seem in need of warmth.
(Croak) She's lucky you like her. Let's save the Queen.
Let me guess your wish, desert child.
You're out of wishes, dreamy prince. I'm coming.
A woman in your condition shouldn't refuse the help of a strong man.
Aye, you're fighting for two. Stand behind me, Mel.
If you'd think a little less and hit a little harder, inventor.
You need to invent yourself a shield, Geppetto.
You need to learn from your near misses.
Aye, you are persistent... but you need to keep that guard up.
Argh... Another fine warrior lost to folly.
I shall miss thee, friend.
You were one who should have stayed at home.
I knew you wouldn't end well.
Ah... my girl... your parting fends my heart.
Scarlet, my girl... You can't die.
You were brave, Piper, I'll give you that. Slow... but brave.
I'll miss your silly tunes, my boy. Go in peace.
Tis a tragic day, my frozen friend.
I shall avenge, thee, my queen of ice.
Go softly to the land of eternal dreams, crazy dreamer.
Twas to be expected, boastful prince.
Melusine! My world is torn assunder.
Melusine! My heart bleeds.
Go in peace, old man. May your mind finally rest.
I thought you'd live forever, old grumpy man. Fare thee well.
To me! To me!
To me, Ravenswatch! We've monsters to expel.
I'm holding, but help would be welcome.
I'm losing ground. I'd welcome some assitance.
I thank thee, guardian of Reverie.
I owe you a favor, friend.
I and my old bones thank thee.
I am in thy debt, friend.
Monsters, nightmares, they all bleed the same.
Drakes and dragons, mine anger burns bright!
They shall sing of our triumphs in the hall of heroes!
I am Beowulf! Prepare to join your ancestors!
Hear me, fathers of my father, today I make you proud!
Fear me, creatures of the night. I am your undoing.
Leave this world to the wise and wanted, foul beasts!
Shield wall! Form the line!
We triumph or we learn! Loss is an illusion... food for the Nightmares.
There is no defeat for the Ravenswatch.
Let me lead the way.
Don't act smart, kid. This could get ugly.
You should.
Wherever there's a nightmare, I'm it's wakeup call.
I was waiting for you, blood tooth. I'm in a sharing mood.
It's the blood of our enemies, lass.
I'm with you, wolf cub.
Aye, 'tis the smell of death and nightmares.
Right behind you, lass.
I could use a good meal myself... after we're finished.
I fight each battle as if it's my last.
You don't know what real fighting is! Back in my day...
Silence rarely bodes anything but danger.
Just be sure to keep behind me.
We're making progress. Slow progress. And your too stubborn to stay at home.
Bite your Pipe, Piper. Watch and learn... Watch and learn!
Wyrm only attacks if provoked.
It's the monsters place to fear us... and yours to scare them. Could you at least try to look a little mean?
The air here reeks of foul mischief.
Those days are behind us, Scarlet... We must endure.
You could never be a foul to me, Mel.
There is a weight to the wind here. Horror has made itself a home.
Is there no place in Reverie that the taint has failed to spoil?
This place has known better days.
What mischief hides its presence? (Croak)
Whatever evil hides here, I will chase it from its hole.
Dragon breath and demon spawn. We've more to free.
Remember to keep your eyes peeled.
There is evil in the wind... do you have its scent?
Aye... There are nightmares in these parts.

My friend, let my story serve as a cautionary tale, if it should serve as one at all. 

Life is made of equal parts joy and sorrow; the greater the one, the deeper the other. 

It's easy to forget when all is well, but the wheel of fortune turns for everyone. You cannot escape what fate has in store for you, but if you're smart, your suffering will make you stronger.

I have known both famine and feast. When I married Princess Badra, life was a beautiful dream for a time. 

Badra. A name as soft and full as the moon itself, rounded and shapely like the figure of my beloved as she lay beside me, swathed in finest silks. 

Her dark-rimmed eyes shone, luminous as stars. Her teeth were like pearls, and her laughter more delightful than wine. Her perfume filled my soul and turned my head, and I forgot for a time that the winds do not blow as ships desire.

One calm and tranquil morning, a traveling merchant appeared at the palace. 

Badra invited him in to rest and offered him a cup of wine to soothe his weary soul. He thanked her for her hospitality and offered her a beautiful lamp as a parting gift.

The moment my beloved laid her delicate finger on the lamp, a storm of sparks surged from inside, enveloping her in a swirl of smoke. 

Badra's ruby lips parted to call for help, but no sound escaped them. She was aspirated into the lamp, which slammed shut with an ominous clang.

In a panic, I tried to pry open the lamp by force, but to no avail. I called the wisest astrologers and magicians to open the lamp, but they assured me in hushed tones there was nothing they could do. 

My beloved Badra was gone, trapped inside the lamp by some dark magic. 

Was I never to taste my beloved's kiss again? Never again listen to her gentle breathing as she slept? Never brush aside a rogue curl that had tumbled over her face as we gazed into one another's eyes?

This cannot be, and it will not be. I am Aladdin, and I am master of my own fate! I swore to find a way to release my Badra from her golden prison, and so I shall! 

I decided to seek out the mysterious witch, Baba Yaga, who is rumored to be the most powerful being in all of Reverie, and enlist her help in restoring my beloved Badra to her true form.

I ventured from our palace in search of the illustrious witch. But I am not a navigator, like Sinbad, and I erred through Reverie like a sleepwalker. 

I kept my beloved's lamp close to me and spoke to her often, whispering sweet nothings and promises of a golden future together once I had freed her. 

In my wanderings, I met an old friend, the Piper, to whom fate had dealt a bitter share. Who among us was left unchanged when the shadow fell over Reverie? 

It is better to walk with a friend in the dark than alone in the light, and Reverie had indeed darkened since last I traveled its roads. 

The Nightmares were as numerous as grains of sand. I joined the Piper in the Ravenswatch, and we battled the evil creatures together, as I sought Baba Yaga. 

The Piper had once known her well, but she hadn't been seen for quite some time. 

My best chance of finding her was by staying with my friend.

The days slipped by like pearls on a silken thread. I never felt closer to Badra than in those quiet moments when I would regale her with the details of the day's battles.

The night brought with it shadows, images that would disturb my slumber. They slipped away from me upon waking like sand through my fingers: Badra, her face contorted in anger. Badra, screaming in pain. Crimson bloodstains on the carpet. Badra, wrapped in a shroud.

Terrifying images. Created by the nightmares, to torment me. But they felt so real...

They became more detailed and more frequent. I began to wonder if I was losing my mind. Was I possessed by the nightmares?

Or was it something worse?

My encounter with the famed Baba Yaga did not go as I had envisioned. Instead of freeing my beloved from her lamp, the witch claimed Badra's fate was beyond her power. Badra could not be freed from the lamp, as she was not in the lamp: Badra was dead.

I refused to believe her; I had seen Badra disappear into the lamp, smelled the magician's sulfur and seen the sparks.

Baba Yaga cackled her evil laugh. Those images were tricks of the mind to lead me into madness. My beloved was deceased, and I was weak, nothing more than a pawn in her games.

Upon hearing her words, the floodgates in my mind opened, and memories of Badra came rushing in. I was overcome with emotion: in keeping out the memories of sadness, I had been holding back on moments of joy as well.

The Witch's taunts released me from the dream that had a hold on my reality. I let go of the dream of Badra I had been clinging to, lest it turn into a nightmare like those I had been fighting.

With my true memories of Badra returned to me, I realized I was all the stronger: for alongside the memory of the pain was the knowledge of our deep love, which is the source of my power. 

Badra shall be with me always, just as she always has been. But today I no longer need the crutch of the lamp to remind me of it.

Together, my beloved and I shall rid the world of the shadows, and one day she and I will be united again for all eternity.

My precious Laura,

My heart had nearly ceased its beating before you wandered so gracefully into my dull and awkward routine. I had read countless stories, and even more poems, about the power of love, but no word, no rhyme, had prepared my soul for the tremor your presence set to rippling through my bones. 

My body ached. My mind ran in circles. For the first time in the billowing of a century, my lips proved incapable of uttering an intelligent thought. Alas, you were merciful, and took me gently by the hand, and after days of torture, worried my affliction was not shared, you offered me a kiss that set my heart aloft.

Your father, so kind to invite me into your home, was the first to stand between us. He could never understand the nature of a creature such as me. His plans for your future were material for a photograph: a husband, a wife, a half-dozen toddlers still clinging to your courageous womb. You wanted a life with me. So we made one and eloped. 

How I miss you, my love. Might these letters bring you back to me, if only in a whisper.

Your eternal love, Carmilla

My precious Laura,

I still feel the warmth of your mischievous gaze each time I miss a button on my blouse or poorly straighten my collar. For twelve short years you were there every morn to assure I looked my best. It was for you and you alone I reddened my lips with carmine. When one walks with a flower it is best to stride in blossom.

I stand firmly even today, with all that has come to pass, on our decision not to turn you into a vampire. Though my powers are formidable, and I do not seem to age, a part of me does fade. I know now, that it is the better part of me that withers. When you were there in my life, my heart and my humanity knew eternal spring. With you gone, the leaves have fallen and the monster inside me demands its due. We had agreed that you would grow old, and how rich and comforting those years of bliss were to me.

Then came the Nightmares and you watched the family and friends you held dear ripped to pieces and their homes ravaged. I must admit, I had forgotten the pang of pain of loss of kin. I had buried my family centuries ago, with all their dreams and mine. Alas, I could never say no to you, and when you begged me to gift you with my affliction in order to help save those remaining, the monster inside me applauded, and the mortal shed a tear.

Your eternal love, Carmilla

My precious Laura,

I had never turned another person before you, either willing or against their will. I was not even sure that I could. I am a day walker, a dhampire, a rare breed of monster that is made in their vampire mother's womb. I was born with this thirst for blood, and never knew the taste of a mother's milk. Your devastation was killing you. Your family castle burned. All those that had raised you nearly dead or worse. And so I let you drink my blood and turned you into a monster.

At first it seemed a good decision. The Ravenswatch accepted us both into their fold and quickly we became a pair of murdering Amazons no other guardian could rival. We avenged your family and drained the blood from both monsters and nightmares. How splendidly you stalked. How deadly you became.

Even when we realized that you could no longer support daylight, it did not diminish our affection. We hunted by night and slept by day in your family's castle vault, the final occupants of your childhood home. I like to think we could have lived centuries in that manner, if we had not crossed paths with old Geppetto, the tinkerer mourning his ravaged son.

Your eternal love, Carmilla

My precious Laura,

When you discovered the old Tinkerer, squeezing the body of his boy in some futile hope that he could bring him back to life, a rage grew inside you only power could quell. You craved faculties only human blood could give you. 

I did not fathom the depth of the wound inside you. I thought your tears for the little boy would dry. Lacerations can heal. Punctures are prone to fester. A needle was lodged within your heart.

You began to disappear at night on longer hunts than was our custom. I could smell the sweetness of human ichor behind your ears and beneath your nails. Your temper grew shorter than candles before the dawn.

I worried. I warned. Blood is a drug, when abused a thirst unquenchable. The pain within your heart had made you deaf to my pleas. The rush of power did the rest. 

And then one day you were gone.

Your eternal love, Carmilla

My precious Laura,

I searched for days with the Watch all of our secret hiding places and nights our favorite hunting grounds. You were nowhere to be found.

Thrice I found the remains of your prey. Your powers had become even more terrifying than my own. Bodies cleaved into several parts. Throats ripped from ear to ear. Heads found a dozen feet from their bodies, with expressions fixed in final terror. The devastation was so complete, and the victims so many, that I could no longer separate the guilty from the innocent. 

Then one night I caught your scent and we tracked you to a mossy clearing in the heart of an ebony wood. You had found a new Pygmalion, the witch Baba Yaga, and she had applauded your transformation.

Beowulf rushed headlong into the trap and fell to your claws. Sun bounced through two nightmares and was brought down by a third. I stood motionless in the onslaught. I could not believe you would attack your own. If it were not for the Snow Queen's ice to defend our retreat, and rescue from the ravens we would have died.

Now I knew you were truly lost, and I had not the slightest clue on how to find you.

Your eternal love, Carmilla

My precious Laura,

Our friends of the Watch left me alone to mourn your betrayal, though I know they shared my pain. I was inconsolable for weeks, wishing I had the disposition to take my own life. An easier darker path began to tease my mind. I could simply join you and the witch, abandoning my human nature, to become a horror alongside the woman I loved.

And so I began to send you letters, asking for you to come and meet me when the moon was at its fullest and the sun its farthest from the dusk and dawn. You joined me in all your splendor, with eyes aglow and hunger in your bosom. We kissed.

I like to think that I saw a last glimmer of your human soul as I drove the wooden stake deep into your heart. The tears in my eyes were playing tricks on my vision. A thousand moments of joy and happiness passed before me as your light went out.

I buried you in your family vault alongside the tombs of those who had raised you. I wept upon your grave, filled with the pain one can only know when one has truly loved. Wherever you had gone, I would soon join you. I set off to kill the Witch.

Your eternal love, Carmilla

My precious Laura,

Defeating Baba Yaga failed to dampen the pain of your loss. If anything it only made me understand how terribly I had failed you. My desire to please you occulted my judgement. I knew better than to turn a soul as pure as your to the dark path. The Witch was only following her chaotic nature. She had abandoned her humanity long ago. I was still half human. I should have protected you from the thirst.

I was about to say as much to you as I visited your grave only to find the tomb empty. Your body was gone without a trace, all save for the stake I had driven through your heart. It sat on a vigil stand with candles still burning. Hope for my future was rekindled in those tiny flames. 

And so I write to you these letters and leave them in your coffin, dreaming that one day you might read them. There is another more selfish reason I write them. For as long as there is a chance you are still alive, I breathe more warmly. Each word I write chases a little farther from my heart the monster within me. 

It is the memory of you that makes me want to carry on. It is the memory of you that keeps me human.


Your eternal love, Carmilla

Once upon a time, I was a happy man. I had everything a humble tinkerer could ever want: a warm workshop, a good reputation, a loving wife, and my greatest treasure of all: a living, laughing son. 

My boy was a farcer, he was, good at scaring, good at hiding and good at all manner of pranks. Red pepper in my stew, rock salt in my shoes, tacks and needles on my chair, and all anger erased by the power of his laugh. His mirth was contagious, the kind to make ribs ache from too much bellowing. 

I have strived to put the memories of my son behind me. They bring pain to my heart, not just a pang akin to hammer hitting finger or nail piercing foot, but a pain that does not disappear.

Alas, this sad story I must tell. I have learned that tears unshed hide from us our brightest riches far more completely than any darkness ever could.

Years of labor and experimentation had led to the unveiling of my masterpiece. The Mayor of Sugarland had asked me for a town clock that would only need winding once a year. I surpassed myself. My town clock not only told the time, but performed a ballet every hour on the hour, danced by autonomous plum fairies to the symphony of an orchestra of animal musicians. 

The mayor stood smiling beside my family as he pulled the lever to unleash the springs of my clever contraption. The clock began to tick, and then whistle and whirl itself to life, as per my careful design. Then it suddenly screeched a sound that was not part of my invention.

Black shadows rose within the tower, and to their chorus my dancers drew knives they should not have had, and my musicians bared teeth I had not made for them. The clock continued ticking as those gathered at the assembly fell dying one by one. Shaking free from my fear during what seemed like an eternity, I took the dead mayor's cane and wedged it into a central gear. The clock died while the Nightmares feasted on our misery.

Night had not yet come when the town militia finally chased the Nightmares from Sugarland. I remember the red sky, glowing like a dying ember through grey ash. My son's body lay where it had fallen, amongst the bodies of the assembly. 

He lay beside his broken mother, a wound to her head, a blow from which she would never awaken. This was a bittersweet blessing, for she was spared from learning that our son had died that night, taken by foul monsters from someone else's vile dreams. She would never have to mourn our proudest creation.

I decided that mourning my wife and child could wait until I had rid Reverie of the creatures that had killed our son. Even were it to take me a lifetime, I would not shed a tear until I had destroyed them all, each and every one.

Once my dead had been buried, I packed my equipment and set out to find the Ravenswatch. They accepted me, and I made the oath. We were a strange lot, but we all had a shared motivation. None would rest until our world was freed of Nightmares.

I had taken pieces and parts from my clock tower with me to study what had gone wrong. The Nightmares had gifted the automatons of my creation with something strange, a pulse of sorts. The metal in their bodies had been magnetized by some kind of electric source, giving them an autonomy akin to a living being. 

Though I did not yet know how to bring about this effect on my own, I had ample supply from the dancers and musicians of my perverted machine to bring doom upon my family. I began to tinker with these pieces and build new playthings of my own. My new toys were not made for children, but rather to avenge their deaths.

Equipped with explosive powders, corrosive acids and poisonous blades, I began to build a metal regiment that Nightmares would learn to fear. My creatures had no heart or soul to stay their hand from the cold tasks at hand. They would do for me what my human heart prevented me from doing myself. My little scoundrels could kill without mercy. I needed only to ask.

I built weapons for the other wardens of the Watch, my favorite a flute for the Piper. My scoundrels performed their duty without question nor complaint. The Nightmares and creatures of the darkness began to fear them, for wherever one came walking, that meant the Ravenswatch were near. 

We wardens shared one thing in common: we hated the Nightmares, for they had taken something precious from each of us. It was after a time that we learned how Baba Yaga had brought these creatures from a dark world into Reverie, and made us each in our own way turn our tools into weapons.

My automatons took damage without pain in these endless fights, and I began to take pride in them. Their courage, I knew, was only the fruit of my own calculated handiwork, but it seemed that strange metal gave a glitter to their eyes. All I knew was that in their wickedness the Nightmares had given me the means to destroy them. Every scoundrel I fabricated took me one step closer to their end.

Though I had seen my scoundrels accomplish many great things, they never stopped surprising me. One morning I noticed that they had begun to share my bunk, though whether to protect me in my sleep or for fear of passing the night alone I am not certain. When the scoundrel I had come to call Cheery-eye brought me a piece of wood to kindle the fire, I was reminded of my son for the first time in uncounted nights. 

I began to take careful notice of my scoundrels' comings and goings. They reminded me of children, minus the mischief, which was the only thing that let me know they were not human. It appeared that they liked me, and though I knew them indestructible, for I could always fix them when they were broken, I found myself worrying for their well-being.

I taught them other tricks besides killing and destruction. Cheery-eye learned to bake a pie. They were not human, I knew it, and their life was due to a dark metal that had given them a simulacre of life. But still, every morning, I would find them near my bed.

Baba Yaga's laughter was not the contagious sort. It was that of someone crazed and desperate, driven to madness by too many shattered dreams. When I finally got the best of her, I asked a simple question. Why do you seek to destroy our peaceful world?

Baba Yaga spoke, "All stories have an age... Reverie fades from the minds of women and men. Something had to be done."

Baba looked at my scoundrels, and a smile softened her crazed face. "You have such beautiful children." To my own surprise, I answered, "I'm proud of each and every one."

I slept that night for the first time with happy dreams of my son and wife. In the morning I awoke surrounded by my scoundrels who had made me breakfast and tea. The eggs were perfect, but the tea was spiked with black pepper. For the very first time I heard my scoundrels laugh.

Most Faithful Nurse,

Would that mine hand had not cause to pen these doleful lines, yet cruel, capricious Fortune doth mock me. Romeo liveth, though I dare not call it a blessing.

By a cruel trick of Fate, my beloved Romeo did not receive the missive from the good Friar detailing his ingenious ruse and news of my feigned death. Thus my love, o’ercome with despair, came to my tomb and thought to join me in eternal sleep. When I awoke, prepared to embrace my love and depart for our golden future, I was dismayed to see that death’s pale flag was planted on his brow.

I grieved as one shattered beyond repair. In my despair, I struck a devil’s bargain. The witch Baba Yaga, whose arts know neither mercy nor limit, hath returned him to me—but not as he once was. His heart knoweth me still, but his memory is a blank slate. Each morning, when my Romeo awakens, he casts a loving gaze upon me, yet remembers naught that transpired afore. He believes it to be the morn after our wedding day, that last peaceful day before this tragedy.

O Nurse, what jest is this, that Death should lay his claim upon my love, then yield him back to me, robbed of his memory? He is here, and yet he is lost. If Heaven be just, why doth it play me thus? Or is justice but a dream, and life naught but a waking sorrow?
Write to me, dear Nurse, though I know not what comfort thou mayst send. If thou hast words to mend a broken soul, send them swift, for I am unmade.

Your loving Juliet

Most Faithful Nurse,

I was surely born under an ill-omened star. Each morn, I apprise Romeo of all that has transpired. Upon learning of his new situation, he has decided to set each day’s occurrences down for his future self in the form of letters, that may serve as a replacement for his now-broken memory. 

He hath taken this new existence in stride, and his demeanour is cheerful. Yet I suffer to see it. Though his step is light and his voice untroubled, I feel terrible guilt, that by my grief, I condemned him to this half-life. That my hand that did clasp his in love hath wrought his undoing, I cannot bear.

O Nurse, how selfish was my love! I did think only of my own grief, my own desolation, and in seeking to mend my heart, I have unmade his very soul. 

Yet I dare not weep, for he is well. He wakes with the sun and sleeps in peace, untroubled by the ghosts that do haunt my every hour. This must be comfort enough, though it doth burn within me like a brand. I have saved his body but stolen his soul, and I cannot make it right.

Pray for me, Nurse, for I am lost.

Your despondent Juliet

Most Faithful Nurse,

I rage, I weep, I plead with Heaven, yet no word of comfort nor sign of hope cometh to ease my troubled heart. I resign myself to the idea that Jove has abandoned me to my fate. I, and I alone, am the sole mistress of my destiny.

And so, I must go to her. I shall seek the wretched crone who hath wrought this curse upon my love and make her undo her wicked craft. I will find her, though I must walk through fire and shadow, though I must beg and crawl and yield all that I am. Let her take all my remaining years, relieve me of my breath, if she will but give him back himself. I care not for the cost, so long as Romeo is whole once more.

Thus we shall leave fair Verona, which has grown far less fair of late, as the shadow of darkness has descended upon it. I know not what evil we shall find beyond our city’s walls, but I am prepared for the worst. I have spent these long weeks honing my skill with the pistol, that Romeo and I may be equal partners on the battlefield, as in life. I am certain now that my hand will not waver when I aim my weapon at the witch and demand that she reverse her spell. When Father taught me to shoot, he thought it simply an amusing pastime; ne’er could he have imagined it would become my only desperate hope. 

Dearest Nurse, if I should fail in my quest, know that I love thee well, and that I did go gladly. For I would rather be dust upon the wind than live to see Romeo lost.

Your wrathful Juliet

Most Faithful Nurse,

The moon doth wax and wane, the sun doth rise and fall, yet naught doth change for us. Each morning Romeo reads his letters, tracing the words with his fingers as if they might awaken some sleeping part of him, but they do not. At night he closes his eyes, and when he wakes, the cycle begins anew.

We have hunted Baba Yaga through darkened woods and whispering shadows. We slay the nightmares together, fighting as one, steel flashing in the dark, yet for every horror vanquished, another doth appear. I fight as one possessed, for if I should falter, he would perish. 

And yet—would it not be a kindness? If I should fall, he would fall as well, and at last be released from this eternal return. Oh, Nurse, I am weary. Not of Romeo, but of this endless, ceaseless turning of days. We do not live—we persist. 

I know not where I shall find the strength to carry on.  And yet—what choice have I? I swore a sacred vow to love him till my dying day, and I would love him still even from beyond the grave. Nothing can separate us, not even the darkest night. If this is all that remains of our dream for a life together, then I shall endure it, for at least he is beside me. At least he is living and whole in body, if not in mind.

I do not know what end awaits us. Until then, I shall walk beside him. Even if I should become but a ghost to him, I would haunt him still.

Your melancholy Juliet

Most Faithful Nurse,

A curious thing hath befallen us. I know not whether ‘tis Fate or mere chance, but for the first time in an age, I feel the stirrings of hope. Not the wild, desperate hope that drove me to seek Baba Yaga’s cruel mercy, nor the hollow hope that dawn might restore remembrance to Romeo’s eyes.

We have found others. They call themselves the Ravenswatch, warriors and wanderers like us, sworn to fight against the darkness, each with a deep wound that doth not heal. In their company, I see that I am not the most forsaken among them. Though I have lost the future I dreamt of, my Romeo lives. There are those who have lost far more.

Romeo doth take to them well, for though his memory is gone, his heart is kind. I have watched them teach and guide him, and though he waketh each morning without memory, he has learnt to trust them. For the first time in an age, I do not feel alone.

I am still uncertain of our future, but no longer do I tread this path in solitude. Perhaps that is enough. This is our life now—fighting, forgetting, and loving anew with each day. But it is a life, Nurse. And after drowning in despair for so long, I think that is no small thing.

Write to me with news of Verona, for though I have found company, none shall ever be so dear to me as thee.

Your hopeful Juliet

Most Faithful Nurse,

O, how blind I have been! How tightly I did cling to what I had lost that I did not see the future unspooling before me. The grief that hath weighed upon my breast was never for Romeo—it was for a dream that cannot be and which I could not let go.

My Romeo is not broken. He is ever the man who ascended to my balcony and won my heart. The fault hath never been in him, but in my refusal to who he hath become. He waketh each day with naught but the words he hath written to himself, yet ne’er doth he waver. He doth not rage against his fate, rather he takes up his sword, laughs with his companions, and presses on. There is no despair in him, only resolve. I who thought myself strong, have in fact been weak all along.

I wish to be brave, to walk beside him, not as a mourner, but as his steadfast partner and his wife. I cannot change the past, but I can stand with him now, laugh with him, dream with him. A different dream. A new dream. Our future shall not be the one I had once woven in my heart, of quiet days and golden years untouched by sorrow. But we have today, and we have each other. That, I see now, is enough.

Dear Nurse, I would have thee know that I am well. At long last, I am ready to walk forward—hand in hand with Romeo, into whatever future may come.

Your grateful Juliet

Most Faithful Nurse,

I scarce know how to set quill to page, for my heart is full beyond measure. Mere words cannot capture a fraction of the joy that hath taken root within me. Once, I did not believe happiness possible, but let this be proof that life doth ever surprise us, if we but open our arms to embrace it.

My love for Romeo was never in doubt, but my feelings of guilt clouded my hope for our future. Romeo's fortitude has shown me the way. He wakes each day as a man unchained by regret, eager to greet the new dawn, and I do the same. We forge each day anew, hand in hand, heart in heart, and what greater proof of love is there than that?

And now, the greatest joy of all—I am with child.

I no longer fear what is to come. Whatever trials await us, we shall face them together and shall find our way, as we always have. And should the child look upon his father and wonder why he must tell his tale anew each day, we shall answer not with sorrow, but with pride. For this child shall grow knowing that his father is the bravest man alive, that he is steadfast and strong, and that his heart knoweth love even when his mind doth not recall its name.

Write to me soon, Nurse, and tell me thou art well. I would have thee near when the child is born, for there is no other hand I would trust to soothe him as thou once didst soothe me.

At last, at long last, I am at peace. And how very sweet it is.

Your loving Juliet

My Yama-uba, old ogress of the wild. I speak to you in my thoughts because here no one hears me.

You raised me like the old mountain Ashigara shelters the forest. You watched me from above among the birds and trees, where the wilderness was free and untamed like me! The animals were my brothers and sisters. I raced deer, laughed with monkeys in the river’s flow. And Kuma taught me to wrestle bears whose shadows swallowed his own. We made the ground tremble with our laughs when I rode him.
I bent trees into bridges, so the villagers could cross the feral river. I made fallen limbs mine to chase away the angry things that had forgotten their names. They fought me with fierce eyes, and I answered with fiercer strength! 

I feared nothing, for I never fought alone. The mountain was with me. And I would forever shelter the mountain, as the mountain had sheltered me!

I can still hear the howling wind from the West, the stillness that followed and the silence swallowing the birds’ song. Clouds darkened the sky and the mountain's shadows stopped dancing across the plains. 

You entrusted us with a message enclosed in a flower and sent us away. 
So I bear Ashigara’s hope, I remember your face and long for my return.

My Yama-Uba. I have seen forests at night. I have met villagers who lost everything. And I have fought fierce beasts who knew no laws!
If you would see what I am seeing here, would you even believe your eyes? 

I did not know the sun could only pierce through Ashigara’s forest canopy. I thought everywhere, monsters and spirits only waited to be healed! 
Here, there is no light to cast  shadows, and the only shadows I know are those resting in my fellow fighters' eyes.
With Kuma at my side, I joined their strange fellowship: a winged onryō afraid of the sun. A maiden made a wolf by night. An old man forced to create yōkai creatures to defend himself.

They say that all things here are wounded and broken. That they are all victims of some dark curse… 

Kuma and I are not!

We follow them, but we do not flicker. Among fireflies humming in rhythm, two steady lights have nothing to say.

We are visitors in this land that does not know your watchful eyes, and we will soon be back home.

Yama-Uba. I remember the day you picked the little golden flower! The mountain and the wind were playing their game: the malicious wind pushed the clouds' shadows across the hillside grass, but the mountain's shadow swallowed them whole. Kuma and I wrestled. You were picking flowers. 
Some you gently plucked from their stem, others you ignored. It only took you one look!
In the shades of the cliffside, you picked the flower who stole the sun’s color. Tightly closed, not yet bloomed. You gently put it in your satchel and refused to tell me if this one was to harm or heal. You only said: 

           “Too much sun will fade the yellow out of it.”

Then the wind howled from the West, and you gave me the flower. It was still sleeping, tight in its petals:

            “Go to the West, give this yamabuki flower to my sister when the time comes, but do not open it until the moment of true need”.

Old ogress of the wild, I know your mischievous eye! And I know better than to ask why the old mountain challenges the wind.

I hid the yamabuki flower in Kuma’s fur! 

If someone tries to reach for it, well… 
They do not know Kuma only hates one thing: it is to be woken up in the middle of his nap. 
They do not know Kuma can make a forest tremble when his stomach is empty. 
And they do not know Kuma’s favorite thing is to wrestle those who try to approach him. 

Kuma takes a lot of naps. Food is hard to find in these empty lands. But my companions are wise enough not to try and pet the bear! I wish someone tried to take the yamabuki flower. I would enjoy watching Kuma wake up!

Yama-Uba, the golden bud is safe and closed tight. I do not even smell it. I will make sure it is untouched until time comes! 

We endure the bare hills and howling islands of this Westland, but we have not found your estranged sister. Yet! Sometimes, I reach for the golden flower inside Kuma’s fur, just to see how yellow it shines! Its bright petals remind me of the mountain’s sunrises.

Yama-Uba. I fight for a reason none of them share. They swore to defeat Baba Yaga. I was sent to bring her a flower.

Do you remember the spirit who took the shape of a giant snake to strangle you while you slept? The yōkai sneaked through the high grass when I jumped in front of it and chopped it to pieces before it could wriggle! 

I do not know how many times the sun rose and set. And finding your strange sister is not fast! The route is filled with stranger kaiju. Kuma and I enjoy fighting these beasts who lost their minds, or maybe they only share one and do not know they are what they are. 
They are not Ashigara's monsters. But I fight them with the same strength, uprooting the rare trees to throw their way, and splitting their mindless heads with my broadaxe!
Here, there are no brothers, no sisters,  to hear my call. Only Kuma, and the little drakeling that follows the big man who forgot how to smile. 

Then I thought! You might have hidden a clue inside the flower. So I sneaked a peek inside Kuma’s fur and saw the yamabuki flower had bloomed! 
I carefully looked inside, and only with my eyes like you taught me! 
Empty.

Empty. No message to be found. Did I lose it? Impossible! Why would you send me here with an empty flower, Yama-Uba? 

Just a yamabuki flower. Fully bloomed. The color of the sun absorbed. The only golden bud to see here. All around us is rotten and bare, and twisted. 

I think I understand now, old ogress of the wild. This tiny flower shines like the sun bouncing on the river in Ashigara. I know that river. I know the giant carp who swims against its current, trying to ascend the waterfall and transform. I rode that fish. How many times did we wrestle beneath the falls, the mighty koi and I? The carp always tries. I always answer.

And I will always be Kintarō, the golden boy of mighty strength! Child of Ashigara who was never meant to carry a message. 

I am the message. I am the yamabuki flower who will always bloom. 
I am the sun who will always rise, no matter the clouds.

Old mother of the wild, we defeated your twisted sister. The others can rest and heal. Some talk about what they lost and gained in the battle. 

I am unchanged. And I want nothing from the witch who stood before me.

I gave her the yamabuki flower. Open and bright! At first, she laughed. 
I just asked her: 

“Do you hear it, old aunt of the shadows? 
The wind in the trees? 
The laughter of the monkeys in the river? 
The breath of the bear? Do you see it, crooked ogress of the West? 
The glowing dance of the fireflies?
And the sun rising over the plains?”

I just reminded her. All those things that do not change. The shadows can hide them, but only for a moment. The sun always pierces through the clouds! 

The only thing that changed, my Yama-Uba, is that now, I know.
